'''Sylvie Méléard''' is a French mathematician specializing in [[probability theory]], [[stochastic process]]es, [[particle system]]s, and [[stochastic differential equation]]s. She is editor-in-chief of ''[[Stochastic Processes and Their Applications]]''.

==Education and career==
Méléard grew up in [[Picardy]] as the daughter of two high school biology teachers, and was already aiming for a career as a mathematician by the time she was ten years old. She studied at the [[Lycée Janson-de-Sailly]] and, from 1977 to 1981, at the {{ill|École normale supérieure de Fontenay-aux-Roses|fr}}, where she became known for [[knitting]] during lectures.{{r|pluton|cv}}
After earning her [[agrégation]] in 1981,{{r|cv}} she completed her doctorate in 1984 at [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] under the supervision of [[Nicole El Karoui]].{{r|mg}}

She took a position at the [[University of Maine (France)|University of Le Mans]], and then moved to Pierre and Marie Curie University as [[maître de conférences]] in 1989. At Pierre and Marie Curie, she earned her [[habilitation]] in 1991. She became a professor at [[Paris Nanterre University]] in 1992, and moved again to the [[École Polytechnique]] in 2006.{{r|pluton|cv}}

==Contributions==
With Vincent Bansaye, Méléard is the author of ''Stochastic Models for Structured Populations: Scaling Limits and Long Time Behavior'' (Springer, 2015).{{r|kaj}} She is also the author of ''Modèles aléatoires en ecologie et evolution'' [''Random models in ecology and evolution''] (Springer, 2016).{{r|whit}}

As of 2018, she is the editor-in-chief of the journal ''[[Stochastic Processes and Their Applications]]'' and, as editor, an executive member in the [[Bernoulli Society]].{{r|bs}}

==Recognition==
In September 2018, a conference on [[population dynamics]] was held at the [[Institut Henri Poincaré]] in honor of Méléard's 60th birthday.{{r|pie}} She was elected to the [[Academia Europaea]] in 2021.{{r|ae}}
